extracted_concepts.name: Product Rule
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: d/dx[f(x)g(x)] = f'(x)g(x) + f(x)g'(x) when f and g are differentiable

extracted_concepts.name: Quotient Rule
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: d/dx[f(x)/g(x)] = [f'(x)g(x) - f(x)g'(x)] / [g(x)]² when g(x) ≠ 0

extracted_concepts.name: Derivative
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: f'(x), the derivative of a differentiable function f, itself a function

extracted_concepts.name: Differentiability
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: hypothesis required on f and g for the Product and Quotient Rules

extracted_concepts.name: Leibniz Notation
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: d/dx(uv) = u'v + uv' and d/dx(u/v) = (u'v - uv')/v²

extracted_concepts.name: Prime Notation
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: f'(x), f''(x), f'''(x) notation for derivatives

extracted_concepts.name: Product Rule for Three Functions
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: d/dx(uvw) = u'vw + uv'w + uvw', extends to three or more functions

extracted_concepts.name: Higher-Order Derivative
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: repeated differentiation: f''', f⁽⁴⁾, etc.

extracted_concepts.name: Second Derivative
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: f''(x) = d²f/dx², the derivative of f' when f' is differentiable

extracted_concepts.name: Third Derivative
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: f'''(x), the derivative of the second derivative

extracted_concepts.name: Position Function
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: s(t), position as a function of time

extracted_concepts.name: Velocity
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: v(t) = s'(t), the first derivative of position

extracted_concepts.name: Acceleration
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: a(t) = s''(t), the second derivative of position

extracted_concepts.name: Jerk
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: s'''(t), the third derivative of position

extracted_concepts.name: Exponential Function
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: e^x, used in Product and Quotient Rule examples; derivative is itself

extracted_concepts.name: Sine Function
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: sin x, differentiated in the Quotient Rule example d/dx(sin x / x)

extracted_concepts.name: Cosine Function
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: cos x, the derivative of sin x appearing in the Quotient Rule example

extracted_concepts.name: Power Function
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: x² and x terms differentiated in the examples (d/dx x² = 2x)

extracted_concepts.name: Product of Functions
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: f(x)g(x) or uv, the form differentiated by the Product Rule

extracted_concepts.name: Quotient of Functions
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: f(x)/g(x) or u/v with g(x) ≠ 0, the form differentiated by the Quotient Rule

extracted_relations.evidence: If f and g are both differentiable, then the Product Rule applies
If f and g are both differentiable and g(x) ≠ 0
The Product Rule can be extended to three or more functions: d/dx(uvw) = u'vw + uv'w + uvw'
If f' is differentiable, f''(x) = d²f/dx² is the derivative of f'
This process can continue to higher orders
continuing the differentiation process one more order
velocity is the first derivative of position
jerk is the derivative of acceleration
d/dx(sin x) = cos x used in d/dx(sin x / x)
x² factor in d/dx(x²e^x) example with d/dx x² = 2x
